channel.title: News Officina
channel.description: Independent. These outlets are written with AI from public sources; one editor reads and approves what goes out. Each says how it is made on its own About page.

item.title: Europa Surgit: One seat, or Europe's security is sold separately
item.description: Moscow wants each NATO country signing its own pact, Finland already said no. A single mandate, carried by Kallas, turns Europe's seat at the next talks into the answer.

item.title: Europae Dexter: Microsoft outage hit email, Teams and police and NHS systems across Europe
item.description: Mapping found 46 of 48 UK police forces and 62 percent of NHS trusts route email through Microsoft 365. Germany's BSI advised backing up critical services with alternatives.

item.title: Europae Laeva: Microsoft outage cut email and Teams across Europe, hitting UK police, health and schools
item.description: Microsoft says the fault came from a network change it has now reversed, and that there was no sign of malicious activity. Nicky Stewart warned the disruption shows the cost of relying on a single cloud provider.

item.title: Europa Surgit: Microsoft 365 outage hit Teams and Exchange as UK police reliance exposed
item.description: Microsoft reversed a network change and worked to restore capacity while 46 of 48 UK police forces were found to route email through the cloud service. The Federal Office for Information Security said there were no indications of a cyberattack.

item.title: Europae Laeva: Japan to raise income tax from 2027 to fund defence build-up
item.description: The government and ruling coalition decided on 18 December to lift the tax in January 2027, while cutting the Reconstruction Special Income Tax by one point. On a single-year basis, the tax burden would not increase for the time being.

item.title: The Harbour Ledger: Japan plans around 60 trillion yen defence spending for fiscal 2027 to 2031
item.description: China calls the plan a push to remilitarise Japan. Tokyo says its defence posture stays exclusively defensive.

item.title: Europa Surgit: Ukraine strikes Volgograd oil refinery
item.description: Analyst Vitaly Vakulenko said the attack puts capacity covering about 55% of Russia's commercial gasoline out of action. Reuters had written several days earlier that about a third of Russian refining capacity was already down.

item.title: Europae Dexter: Volgograd strike puts 55% of Russia's gasoline capacity out of action, Vakulenko says
item.description: Analyst Vitaly Vakulenko says commercial gasoline production is hit after Ukraine struck the Lukoil plant, one of the key fuel stations for Russia's army in the south according to Ukraine's General Staff. Two industry sources told Reuters refining capacity is down roughly 30% since strikes resumed.

item.title: Europae Laeva: Analyst says Ukrainian strikes put about 55% of Russia's petrol refining out of action
item.description: The attack on Lukoil's Volgograd refinery has left 114 apartment buildings in Rostov-on-Don without heating, and Rosneft has reinstated fuel sales limits as queues form at petrol stations.

item.title: Europa Patriarum: Ukraine strikes Volgograd refinery as analyst says 55% of Russian gasoline output is down
item.description: The Lukoil plant, processing about 15 million tonnes of oil a year, burned after an overnight drone attack, and Rosneft has reinstated fuel sale limits nationwide. Strikes since late October have hit refineries with about 30% of Russia's primary refining capacity.

item.title: Europa Surgit: Poland took Russia's seat at the UN. Make that Europe's habit.
item.description: One European campaign beat a sixty-year Russian hold on a UN post, by a single vote. EU governments should agree a common candidate before every future contest, so one flag fields it and all of them fight for it.

item.title: The Harbour Ledger: Europe gets a seat at the next Ukraine talks, but not the deal
item.description: Trump's envoy Kushner announced the move on Thursday, and the Kremlin at once played it down. EU foreign policy chief Kallas said the US cannot negotiate lifting sanctions on Europe's behalf.

item.title: Europa Surgit: The design door is open. Now legislate the factory floor.
item.description: From early 2027 imec's pilot line hands European designers the tools to model leading-edge chips. Parliament and the Council must keep their own mid-2027 date and pass Chips Act 2.0, so those designs are made in Europe.

item.title: Europae Dexter: Japan to revise security documents a year early, weighing 50 to 60 trillion yen plan
item.description: The revision expands defence spending from fiscal 2027, below the Defense Ministry's own estimate, with Beijing objecting in advance to any renewed naming of China as Japan's chief challenge.

item.title: Europae Laeva: Quantum Systems drone fleet flying again after cyberattack on update server
item.description: The Bundeswehr had grounded a large share of the fleet as a precaution, the Financial Times reported, and federal authorities are investigating the attack that Der Spiegel reported reached Bundeswehr servers before anyone detected it.

item.title: Europae Dexter: Russia suspected after cyberattack grounded Bundeswehr Quantum Systems drones
item.description: German forces briefly suspended flights of Quantum Systems' Vector drones amid an investigation into hostile actors, with the BfV having warned of risks to firms supporting Ukraine.

item.title: Nuntii Europae: Finland's Parliament to vote on extending border security law to end of 2028
item.description: The Constitutional Committee proposes handling the bill under the constitutional enactment procedure, allowing approval by a two-thirds majority. The Social Democratic Party will vote in favour.

item.title: Europae Dexter: Slovak president calls for electricity prices to be cut from gas
item.description: Peter Pellegrini made the case after talks with Emmanuel Macron in Paris, as the EU debate over electricity market reform continues.

item.title: Nuntii Europae: US says Europe will join next Ukraine talks as EU argues over who represents it
item.description: Jared Kushner, the US envoy, said Moscow and Kyiv had agreed to bring European countries in, and Russia and the US want Europe to name one person to deal with Russia. Kaja Kallas and António Costa have put themselves forward.

item.title: Europae Laeva: Slovakia and France team up to push for power bills decoupled from gas prices
item.description: President Peter Pellegrini called the EU's gas-linked pricing illogical for a country that does not depend on gas for its electricity. The visit also brought a 120 million euro helicopter deal and talks on defence cooperation.

item.title: Leo Batavus: Nordic defence ministers agree to develop a joint defence agreement
item.description: The decision of 12 November 2026 would give the Nordic defence cooperation a legal framework. Separately, the Riksdag voted to raise the military service age limit to 47, effective 1 January 2027.

item.title: Nuntii Europae: Slovak and French presidents call for overhaul of EU electricity pricing
item.description: Peter Pellegrini and Emmanuel Macron met in Paris for their first bilateral talks, with a 120 million euro contract for three Airbus helicopters signed in the days around the meeting.

item.title: Nuntii Europae: EU leaders gather in Dublin to debate who speaks for Europe in Ukraine talks
item.description: The debate, called at Italy's request, will not produce a name before December. Poland objects to western Europe negotiating over the east, while Estonia says the existing envoys are enough.

item.title: Nuntii Europae: US Treasury Secretary moves to military base after death threats linked to Iran
item.description: The United States has also moved refuelling aircraft from a British air base to Germany and other locations, and charged three men accused of plotting an attack on another British base on behalf of Iran's Revolutionary Guard.

item.title: Europa Patriarum: France blames Iran's Revolutionary Guard for cyber attack on 700 retail sites
item.description: Paris will propose further sanctions against Iranian entities to its European partners. A Commission spokesperson said it is not the Commission's role to attribute cyber incidents. Iran rejects the accusations, and Paris prosecutors are seeking international arrest warrants.

item.title: Leo Batavus: EU auditors say uneven enforcement blunts Russia sanctions
item.description: Direct trade with Russia fell from 253 billion euros to 58 billion between 2021 and 2025. The European Court of Auditors calls for clearer rules and stronger monitoring, saying the Commission lacks criteria to judge whether the sanctions work.

item.title: The Harbour Ledger: EU sanctions cut Russia trade to 58 billion euros but enforcement lags
item.description: Trade fell from 253 billion euros in 2021. The European Court of Auditors says unclear rules and uneven application let firms bypass the bans, and Russia now trades more with India and China.

item.title: Europa Patriarum: Portugal rebukes NATO chief Rutte over 'flippant' missile remarks
item.description: The foreign ministry in Lisbon objected to remarks suggesting the government downplays the Russian threat, as Spain stayed silent.

item.title: Attacotti: ESET links Cereal email malware found at Romanian agency to Russia-aligned Turla
item.description: The security firm says the toolset, run on Microsoft Exchange, was set up to collect emails involving NATO and EU addresses. A Kazakh government body was also compromised, and ESET reads that hit as surveillance of Russian dissidents.

item.title: The Harbour Ledger: Launch the Black Sea mission while Turla sits in government mail
item.description: A toolset built to filter NATO and EU correspondence sat on a Romanian government server, and Romania has asked for exactly this mission. Europe's governments should launch it and pay for cyber defence of ports and shipping lanes inside it.
